headline: THE ONE 'INTERESTED: YES' ON 355 COMANCHE FINALLY HAS A NAME AND A PHONE NUMBER — Angela B. at Keller Williams Vestavia, whose only objection was the price at $299,000, a number that came down to $295,000 three days later and nobody ever told her. Her call task is on your board now. And the listing that four agents refused to price just booked TWO showings for this weekend.

hotSignals.signal: 🔎 IDENTIFIED THIS MORNING AFTER SIX DAYS AS AN ANONYMOUS ROW. Angela B. · Keller Williams Realty Vestavia filed the only 'interested: YES' this listing has ever taken — priced TOO HIGH against the $299,000 list, staging 4 of 5, and one line of free text that changes how you play it: "Saw another home that she is interested in." ⭐ HER SINGLE STATED OBJECTION HAS ALREADY BEEN ANSWERED — the price came down to $295,000 on 8/5 and she was never told. ⚠️ SHE ALSO NEVER NAMED A REPLACEMENT NUMBER, same as every other read on this file.
hotSignals.action: Call her — the task is on your board with her full contact details. Two questions carry it: is that other house under contract yet, and what gets her buyer in this one. Quote $295,000 and nothing else; no agent has ever put a different number on paper here.

hotSignals.signal: ✅ YOU CLOSED THIS ONE LAST NIGHT. Mallory W. · ARC Realty filed the board's only unqualified yes — interested YES, priced JUST RIGHT, her buyer wants to write and is short on down payment and nothing else — and you checked the call off at 11:35 PM. ⚠️ THE DECISION UNDERNEATH IT IS STILL OPEN AND STILL YOURS: you have not asked your seller for a concession number, so there is nothing to trade with yet.
hotSignals.action: No new call needed — this is now a seller call, not an agent call. Same seller owns Lake Crest and Martinwood: three files, one phone call.

upcoming: 📅 SUN 8/9 · 1:30 PM — 355 COMANCHE ST, Montevallo. ⭐ BOOKED AT 10:27 LAST NIGHT and it is the newest thing on this entire board. It also lands the day BEFORE the appointment you were already counting on.

📅 MON 8/10 · 1:40 PM — 355 COMANCHE ST, Montevallo. Booked Friday morning. ⭐ TWO WEEKEND SHOWINGS ON THE LISTING THAT FOUR AGENTS REFUSED TO PRICE — after a fortnight where a single booking was news. Treat the pair as the real tiebreaker on price-problem versus presentation-problem.
⭐ ALSO WORTH KNOWING: a teammate's buyer asked to see 355 Comanche and is working on pre-approval. Not booked in the system, so it will not appear here until it is.

listings.status: 🔥 ACTIVE — the quietest listing on the board just booked two showings in two days, and its one YES now has a name

feedback.note: 🔴 THE READ YOU WAITED ALL WEEK FOR, filed 3:13 PM Friday off Thursday's 11:00 AM tour — the first fresh booking since the price cut. Interested: NO. Staging 3 of 5. ⛔ THE DECISIVE PART IS THE BLANKS: 'is it priced right' — blank. 'price change recommendation' — blank. 'what price' — blank. 'main thing' — blank. An agent who thinks a house is overpriced usually says so; this one declined to say anything at all.

🔎 THE ANONYMOUS ROW, NAMED THIS MORNING. Interested: YES. Priced TOO HIGH against the $299,000 list. Staging 4 of 5 — the best staging score this listing has ever taken, and it undercuts the theory that presentation is the whole problem. ⭐ HER FREE TEXT IS THE PART THAT MATTERS: "Saw another home that she is interested in." That is a cross-shopping buyer, not a rejection — and her price objection was answered three days later by the cut to $295,000, which she was never told about. ⚠️ Like every other agent on this file, she left 'what price' blank.

listings.note: ⛔ THE PRICE-QUOTE RULE IS UNCHANGED AND IT MATTERS MORE NOW THAT YOU ARE CALLING AN AGENT: quote $295,000 and nothing else. Across four written reads and one agent preview, not one agent has ever put a different number on paper — every 'what price' field is empty. There is no market-supported replacement price to quote, so quoting one would be inventing it. ⭐ WHAT THE PATTERN SAYS: three reads called it too high at $299,000; since the cut to $295,000, the two reads that followed stopped saying it. ⭐ AND THE STAGING SCORES DISAGREE WITH EACH OTHER — 4 of 5 from Angela B., 3 of 5 from Ashton J. That is a listing without a clear defect, which usually means traffic is the fix. ✅ TRAFFIC ARRIVED: two showings this weekend, Sunday and Monday.

listings.status: 🔥 ONE TERM FROM CONTRACT — the close-date answer is now roughly 22 hours overdue

feedback.note: 🔥 NOT A FEEDBACK FORM — A DEAL. At 9:05 Friday morning he wrote that the buyers agree to ALL of the counter's new terms with one exception: they want to close on or before Oct 23 rather than Oct 30, because they have four kids and moving the week of Halloween will not work. ⭐ Price agreed. Concession agreed. Co-op agreed. Appliances agreed. ⚠️ HE THEN CHASED IT HIMSELF at 2:51 PM — "any update on the closing date ask?" ⏰ AS OF THIS MORNING THE ANSWER IS ABOUT 22 HOURS OVERDUE and no outbound to him appears in mail or the text relay. Stated as ABSENCE, not failure: a phone call leaves no trace here.
🔥 WROTE THE OFFER. Contract, pre-approval letter and a personal letter from the buyers, submitted 3:15 PM, followed by his own text eleven minutes later.

Answered your direct email inside the hour: his buyer is passing, there were "many aspects of the house that she loved but was just hoping for a bit of a 'larger' feel." A near miss on SHAPE, not price.
Filed interested NO off the same-day 6:15 PM booking — from the agent who then wrote the offer three days later. ⭐ A reminder that a filed 'no' is a snapshot of one moment, not a verdict.

gaps: Two of the four tours in the window never produced a written read — but this listing has since produced an offer, so chasing them is no longer the point.
listings.note: 🔥 THE SHOWING BOARD'S JOB ON THIS FILE IS DONE — it converted. Fourteen days, four tours, five written reads, one offer, one counter, one acceptance-but-for-a-date. ⭐ THE ONE THING THIS BOARD CAN STILL TELL YOU: the date is a SELLER decision, not yours. You asked for Oct 30 deliberately because the sellers' new build lands inside that window, so the sequence is seller first, then Robert. Either date closes inside 2026 and counts against the 45.

Two public prices is a bigger risk than a slow sale, and it is two minutes to check. ⭐ Same seller as Altamont and Lake Crest — one phone call covers all three.

oweFeedback.when: 🔴 ASKED THREE TIMES — Thu 7/30, Fri 7/31, Sat 8/1 — from the Keller Williams Realty Hoover listing side after your 7/30 tour, and you have since CLOSED on the property AND BEEN PAID. ⭐ STILL THE MOST OVERDUE ITEM ON THE BOARD in relationship terms, and getting paid sharpened it. Before the closing it read as an oversight; after completing a deal together and collecting on it, it reads as a shrug at the agent across the table. ⚠️ Their last request is now a week old and the listing has gone EXPIRED in their system — the window where feedback is still useful to them is closing. Thirty seconds, and the same message carries the two answers you actually want back.
